season|2024]]) }} '''Gabriel Ifeanyi "Iffe" Lundberg''' (born 4 December 1994) is a Danish professional [[basketball]] player for [[Maccabi Tel Aviv B.C.|Maccabi Tel Aviv]] of the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League]] and the [[EuroLeague]].{{Cite news|url=https://partizan.basketball/vesti/aktuelno/3734|title=Iz crno-bele Bolonje u crno-beli Beograd: Ife Lundberg je novi košarkaš Partizana Mozzart Bet|newspaper=Normacore.com |language=sr|access-date=June 20, 2024 |last1=Normasoft. Net |first1=Normasoft }} He also represents the [[Denmark men's national basketball team|Denmark national team]]. Standing at {{height|m=1.93}}, he can play at both [[Guard (basketball)|guard]] positions. According to numerous Danish outlets, Lundberg is Denmark's best basketball player.[https://ekstrabladet.dk/sport/anden_sport/anden_sport/gigantisk-dansk-triumf-slaar-barcelona/8179027 Gigantisk dansk triumf: Slår Barcelona] Jonas Ryefelt (Ekstra Bladet), 26 June 2020. Accessed 13 July 2020. {{in lang|da}}{{Cite web|url=https://sport.tv2.dk/basketball/2021-12-07-dansker-foeler-sig-sikker-paa-nba-jeg-var-ekstremt-eftertragtet|title=Danmarks bedste basketballspiller tror stadig på NBA|website=[[TV 2 (Denmark)|TV 2]]|language=da|date=December 21, 2021|access-date=March 13, 2022}} ==Professional career== ===Early career (2013–2019)=== Lundberg started his professional basketball career in the Danish [[Basketligaen]] playing for [[Falcon Basketball|Falcon]] (2013–14), [[BMS Herlev Wolfpack]] (2014–15) and [[Horsens IC|Horsens]] (2015–2017),[https://basketligaen.dk/stats/?WHurl=%2Fperson%2F172095%3F Gabriel Iffe Lundberg] before moving to Spanish [[LEB Oro]] team [[Bàsquet Manresa|Manresa]]. He helped Manresa return to the [[Liga ACB]] in his first season. ===Canarias (2019–2020)=== In July 2019, Lundberg signed with [[CB Canarias]] for two years with the option of a third. He joined the team from the competitor [[Bàsquet Manresa]] where he had been a cornerstone of the team that won promotion to the [[Liga ACB]].[https://www.marca.com/baloncesto/acb/2019/07/09/5d247f2446163f76368b459c.html Gabriel Lundberg cambia Manresa por Tenerife para seguir en la ACB] Marca.com, 9 July 2019. Accessed 13 July 2020. {{in lang|es}} ===Zielona Góra (2020–2021)=== On 13 July 2020, Lundberg signed with [[Basket Zielona Góra|Stelmet Zielona Góra]] of the [[Polish Basketball League|Polish League]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.eurobasket.com/Poland/news/635633/Stelmet-Enea-inks-Gabriel-Lundberg|title=Stelmet Enea inks Gabriel Lundberg|last=|first=|date=July 13, 2020|website=Eurobasket.com|publisher=|language=En|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=July 14, 2020}} He averaged 20.4 points, 3.8 rebounds, 5.4 assists and 1.4 steals per game in the [[VTB United League]] during the 2020–21 season.{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Iffe Lundberg is the first Dane in CSKA!|url=https://cskabasket.com/en/news/n/iffe-lundberg-signed-with-cska/|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2021-02-15|website=CSKA Moscow Basketball}} ===CSKA Moscow (2021–2022)=== On February 15, 2021, he left Zielona Gora and signed with [[PBC CSKA Moscow|CSKA Moscow]] for the rest of the season.{{Cite news|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/cska-moscow-announces-iffe-lundberg/|title=Cska Moscow announces Iffe Lundberg|last=|first=|date=February 15, 2021|website=|newspaper=Sportando|language=En|access-date=February 15, 2021 |last1=Maggi |first1=Alessandro }} On July 2, 2021, Lundberg signed a three-year (2+1) extension with the Russian club. On February 27, 2022, upon the outbreak of the [[2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine]], he left the team.{{Cite web |date=February 26, 2022 |title=Tornike Shengelia leaves CSKA Moscow: I can't play for the Russian army club |url=https://www.marca.com/en/basketball/2022/02/26/621a42cd22601db64a8b45b6.html |website=MARCA}}{{Cite web |title=5 CSKA Moscow players leave team for war between Russia, Ukraine |url=https://www.aa.com.tr/en/russia-ukraine-crisis/5-cska-moscow-players-leave-team-for-war-between-russia-ukraine/2518369 |website=www.aa.com.tr}}{{Cite web |last=Amico |first=Sam |date=March 1, 2022 |title=FIBA Suspends All Russian Teams, Officials From Competition |url=https://hoopswire.com/fiba-suspends-all-russian-teams-officials-from-competition/}} The team accused him of violating his contract.{{Cite web |title=CSKA confirms departures of Shengelia, Voigtmann, Grigonis and Lundberg |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/euroleague/1314141/cska-confirms-departures-of-shengelia-voigtmann-grigonis-and-lundberg/ |date=February 27, 2022|access-date=February 28, 2022 |website=Eurohoops}} ===Phoenix Suns (2022)=== On March 12, 2022, the [[Phoenix Suns]] signed Lundberg to a [[two-way contract]] for the rest of the 2021–22 season.{{cite web|first=Johnny |last=Askounis|url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/nba-news/1319246/danish-star-gabriel-lundberg-reportedly-inks-deal-with-suns/|website=Eurohoops.net|title=Lundberg inks deal with Suns|date=March 12, 2022|access-date=March 12, 2022}} He subsequently became the first Danish player in history to sign an NBA contract. However, he did not make his NBA debut until April 3 against the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] due to visa issues that stemmed from the [[2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine]].{{cite web | url=https://www.12news.com/article/sports/nba/suns/suns-guard-becomes-first-danish-player-nba/75-1263f8ee-19ec-4080-b4de-7b0b1fedd885 | title=Suns guard becomes first Danish player to play in NBA | date=April 5, 2022 }} In the final game of the regular season, Lundberg recorded season-highs of 10 points, 5 rebounds, and 5 assists in a loss to the [[Sacramento Kings]].{{cite web | url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/boxscores/202204100PHO.html | title=Kings vs Suns, April 10, 2022 }} ===Virtus Bologna (2022–2024)=== On July 21, 2022, Lundberg signed a two-year deal with [[Virtus Bologna]] of the Italian [[Lega Basket Serie A]] (LBA) and the [[EuroLeague]].{{cite web|url=https://www.virtus.it/news/gabriel-lundberg-e-un-nuovo-giocatore-di-virtus-segafredo-bologna/|website=virtus.it|title=Gabriel Lundberg è un nuovo giocatore di Virtus Segafredo Bologna!|date=July 21, 2022|access-date=July 21, 2022}} On 29 September 2022, after having ousted [[Olimpia Milano]] in the semifinals, Virtus won its [[2022 Italian Basketball Supercup|third Supercup]], defeating 72–69 [[Dinamo Sassari|Banco di Sardegna Sassari]] and achieving a back-to-back, following the 2021 trophy.{{cite web |title=Supercoppa, trionfa la Virtus Bologna! Canestro decisivo di Mickey, Sassari cede 72-69|url=https://www.gazzetta.it/Basket/SerieA/29-09-2022/basket-supercoppa-trionfa-virtus-bologna-sassari-ko-72-69-450409276762.shtml|website=Gazzetta dello Sport|date=29 September 2022}} However, despite good premises Virtus ended the [[2022–23 EuroLeague|EuroLeague season]] at the 14th place, thus it did not qualify for the playoffs.[https://bolognabasket.org/virtus-il-punto-a-fine-eurolega/ Virtus, il punto a fine EuroLega]. BolognaBasket Moreover, the team was defeated in the [[Italian Basketball Cup]] final by [[Pallacanestro Brescia|Brescia]]. In June, after having ousted 3–0 both Brindisi and Tortona, Virtus was defeated 4–3 by Olimpia Milan in the national finals, following a series which was widely regarded among the best in the latest years of Italian basketball.[https://video.repubblica.it/sport/basket-milano-batte-bologna-nella-decisiva-gara-7-e-vince-il-suo-30esimo-scudetto-gli-highlights/447915/448883 Basket, Milano batte Bologna nella decisiva gara 7 e vince il suo 30esimo scudetto. Gli highlights]. la Repubblica[https://www.rainews.it/articoli/2023/06/basket-serie-a-playoff-olimpia-milano-batte-virtus-bologna-in-gara-7-e-vince-lo-scudetto-al-forum-assago-c279332e-c2fa-46be-a199-3ff966b78a99.html Basket, Milano batte Bologna 67-55 nella finalissima e si conferma campione per la trentesima volta]. Rai News On 24 September 2023, after having ousted Olimpia Milano in the semifinals, Virtus won its [[2023 Italian Basketball Supercup|fourth Supercup]], and the third in a row, defeating 97–60 [[Pallacanestro Brescia|Germani Brescia]].[https://bologna.repubblica.it/sport/2023/09/24/news/una_virtus_esagerata_stravince_la_supercoppa-415671857/ Una Virtus esagerata stravince la Supercoppa]. la Repubblica ===Partizan (2024–2025) === On June 20, 2024, Lundberg signed a two-year deal with [[KK Partizan|Partizan Mozzart Bet]] of the [[Basketball League of Serbia]] (KLS), [[ABA League]] and the [[EuroLeague]]. During the 2024–25 season, Partizan managed to lift the record eighth [[2024–25 ABA League First Division|ABA League]] championship, and the [[2024–25 Basketball League of Serbia|Serbian League]] championship, the first one after 11 seasons. On November 8, 2025, Lundberg left the team after not playing at all during the 2025-2026 season.{{cite web |title=Iffe Lundberg says goodbye to Partizan |url=https://basketnews.com/news-234632-iffe-lundberg-says-goodbye-to-partizan.html |website=basketnews.com |access-date=13 November 2025 |language=en}} ===Maccabi Tel Aviv (2025-present)=== On November 10, 2025, Lundberg joined [[Maccabi Tel Aviv B.C.]] after parting ways with Partizan,{{cite web |title=Iffe Lundberg officially joins a new team in EuroLeague |url=https://basketnews.com/news-234544-iffe-lundberg-maccabi-partizan.html |website=basketnews.com |access-date=13 November 2025 |language=en}} but he came in to the season with a minor injury so he was unable to start right away. {{cite web |title=Maccabi new signing sidelined with injury |url=https://basketnews.com/news-234755-maccabi-new-signing-sidelined-with-injury.html |website=basketnews.com |access-date=12 November 2025 |language=en}} In July 2026, Lundberg reached an agreement with the team on a new three year contract.{{cite web |title=Maccabi retain key EuroLeague guard on new deal |url=https://basketnews.com/news-252689-maccabi-retain-iffe-lundberg-on-new-long-term-deal.html |website=basketnews.com |access-date=28 July 2026 |language=en}} ==National team== [[File:Gabriel Lundberg.jpg|thumb|Lundberg, 2016.]] Lundberg has been a member of the [[Denmark men's national basketball team]]. In November 2020, he led the team to two consecutive surprise victories against favorites Lithuania and the Czech Republic in the qualification round to the European championships. Lundberg had 28 points in the win against Lithuania{{Cite web|last=Ghoula|first=Benjamin|date=2020-11-27|title=Danmark tager sensationel sejr over Litauen {{!}} Fullcourt.dk|url=https://www.fullcourt.dk/landshold/danmark-tager-sensationel-sejr-over-litauen/|access-date=2020-12-01|website=Fullcourt|language=da-DK}} which was named arguably the greatest victory in Danish basketball history.{{Cite web|last=Hald|first=Benjamin Nielsen|date=2020-11-27|title=Danmark var historisks store underdogs {{!}} Fullcourt.dk|url=https://www.fullcourt.dk/landshold/danmark-var-historisk-store-underdogs/|access-date=2020-12-01|website=Fullcourt|language=da-DK}} Against the Czech team, he scored 38 points, knocking down 7-of-9 from three-point range.{{Cite web|last=Bonde|first=Sebastian Würtz|date=2020-11-29|title=Danmark besejrer sensationelt Tjekkiet i sand gyser {{!}} Fullcourt.dk|url=https://www.fullcourt.dk/landshold/danmark-besejrer-sensationelt-tjekkiet-i-sand-gyser/|access-date=2020-12-01|website=Fullcourt|language=da-DK}} ==Personal life== Lundberg is a native of [[Copenhagen]]. He is of Nigerian and Danish descent.{{Cite web |title=Gabriel Iffe Lundberg NBA |url=https://www.888sport.dk/blog/gabriel-iffe-lundberg-nba |access-date=2026-07-20 |website=www.888sport.dk |language=da}} In the early years, he played [[3x3 basketball|3x3 streetball]] at the local street courts in Vesterbro, the Copenhagen neighborhood in which he grew up.{{Cite web |title=Official Les Deux Brandsite & Online Store |url=https://lesdeux.com/blogs/explore/gabriel-iffe-lundberg-behind-the-backboard |access-date=2026-07-20 |website=Les Deux |language=en}} He was a regular at the GAME Finals Streetball Tournament at the Town Hall Square each summer and watched from the stands, when his older brother Abdel Jaleel Lundberg competed in the Elite Division and the Slam Dunk Contest, winning it several times. Iffe later joined Falcon Basketball Club where he played during most of his childhood.{{Cite web |title=Iffe Lundberg Profile |url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/euroleague/players/iffe-lundberg/profile/010781/ |url-status=dead |website=www.euroleaguebasketball.net |language=en-GB}} In the off-season Iffe would come back to play streetball and won in 2009 2nd place at the GAME Finals Streetball Tournament with his
